## Purpose and boundary

`form.references` describes correspondences between reference catalogues, for both code lists and registries.

Business calculations, related-record navigation and destination-row creation belong to the exporter API.

The exporter keeps those decisions in configuration and registered functions, outside its generic execution engine.

See [Export design](../export-design.html) for the overall workflow.

The [LL reference inventory][inventory] records catalogue-specific evidence and decisions.

[inventory]: ../04-references-code-lists/ll-reference-correspondences.html

## Independent schema and configuration

The neutral schema is `form.references/inst/schema/mapping-1.0.0.yaml`.

It is separate from the reference-catalogue configuration schema.

The concrete ObServe 10.0 to ROS LL 4.2.0 file is `inst/10.0/ll/4.2.0/mapping.yaml`.

The source configuration is `inst/10.0/ll/references.yaml`, registered by the caller as `observe`.

The gear's source model and SQL queries are shared across its ROS form versions.

```yaml
schema_version: "1.0.0"

catalogues:
  source: {configuration: observe, catalogue: code_lists, lookup: topiaid}
  target: {configuration: ros, catalogue: code_lists, lookup: code}

mappings:
  refs_fishery.light_colours:
    source:
      table: ll_common.lightstickscolor
    file: correspondences/refs_fishery.light_colours.csv

  refs_admin.countries:
    source:
      table: common.country
      property: iso3code

  refs_biology.species:
    source:
      table: common.species
      property: faocode

  refs_biology.predator_species:
    source:
      table: common.species
      property: faocode
```

`configuration` selects a reference configuration registered by the caller under that name.

`catalogue` selects its `code_lists` or `registries` entry without duplicating the catalogue definition.

The ROS target table name is the mapping entry point; `source.table` identifies the ObServe source catalogue table.

Source remains ObServe and target remains ROS. Values always translate from ObServe to ROS.

Use one object for a single source mapping and a list of alternatives if a target accepts several source mappings.

Select by the supplied source identity and effective lookups; never choose the first alternative automatically.

The list is not a sequence of transformations or a fallback order.

Separate target entries for general and predator species both declare `common.species` as their source.

Weight measurements and fish-processing types likewise declare `common.weightmeasuretype`, with separate CSV files.

## Target-driven selection

The exporter starts from the ROS model field's target reference.

It selects the corresponding mapping and supplies the ObServe value together with its source catalogue table.

```text
ROS field requires refs_biology.predator_species / code
  -> select mappings.refs_biology.predator_species
  -> receive an ObServe common.species technical ID
  -> find the source record and read faocode
  -> resolve the value in refs_biology.predator_species
  -> return its code
```

The exporter declares which source record field supplies the value; the catalogue mapping does not navigate records.

## Defaults and correspondence sources

The catalogue selections declare default source and target lookups.

An entry's `source.lookup` overrides the source default; its `lookup` overrides the target default.

The entry's omitted `property` defaults to its effective target lookup, normally `code` for ROS code lists.

There is no `mode` or nested `correspondence` property.

Choose at most one of `source.property` and `file`; omitting both sends the input unchanged to the target lookup.

### Explicit correspondence: direct

`file` identifies a CSV with `source_value,target_value` columns, both read as text.

For these ObServe declarations, `source_value` contains technical IDs, not business codes such as `B` or `CH`.

`target_value` contains a ROS code submitted to the selected target lookup.

```text
Supplied light-colour topiaId
  -> explicit CSV correspondence
  -> ROS light-colour lookup on code
  -> canonical target code
```

There is no source lookup. The target lookup applies its own catalogue aliases and configured matching behaviour.

Relative file paths resolve beside `mapping.yaml`.

Repeated identical pairs are equivalent; different target values for one source value are ambiguous.

An absent correspondence remains unresolved. It does not silently fall back to the original technical ID.

### Source property: rebound

`source.property` identifies the value to read after finding the source record with its effective lookup.

```text
Supplied species topiaId
  -> source common.species lookup on topiaid
  -> read faocode
  -> selected ROS species lookup on code
  -> canonical target code
```

Both catalogue lookups include their existing aliases.

The `RMJ -> RMM` alias belongs to `refs_biology.species`; it is not a correspondence added to this mapping.

Do not assume that another target list, including predator species, owns the same aliases.

Source lookup names must match the registered reference configuration exactly; there is no implicit column renaming.

Port conversion is an export business rule, outside this catalogue-mapping file.

The rule uses the ObServe harbour's `locode` to determine a candidate ROS port code.

`form.references` then resolves that code through the existing `refs_admin.ports` lookup on `code`.

This does not add a function mechanism or require a UN/LOCODE column in the ROS catalogue.

## LL 4.2.0 coverage

The model declares 47 code lists used by 128 fields, plus four registries used by 11 fields.

The file covers the 14 target lists selected from the inventory's lookup and recoding categories.

It declares four source-property mappings and ten CSV correspondences.

Those 14 target entries use 12 source tables; species and weight-measurement types each supply two targets.

The ten CSV declarations keep explicit correspondence values separate from the mapping structure.

Files are named after their ROS target table: `correspondences/schema.table.csv`.

They contain 28 initial pairs drawn from values encountered in the 70 saved trips from 2020–2025.

The sibling `correspondences-extended/` set adds 14 catalogue candidates, including unused historical values.

It contains the original pairs too; `mapping.yaml` continues to select only `correspondences/`.

Each directory's README records its scope, remaining gaps and target catalogue ambiguities.

The 21 export-rule lists include ports; 12 lists require source information to be identified.

Registry identity mapping remains separate from this code-list configuration.

## Validation and resolution

Validate the YAML structure and lookup defaults without loading catalogue data.

Check declared configuration, catalogue, table and lookup names separately from actual record resolution.

Check column availability and correspondence CSV contents when the relevant data are loaded.

Only property-based mappings require source catalogue data; file-based mappings do not perform a source lookup.

All catalogue lookups use exact matching, then catalogue aliases, then configured normalized-name matching.

Normalized names are comparison keys, not proof of identity. Preserve multiple matching records as candidates.

Check only encountered reference values, grouped by selected target mapping and source table.

Unused source catalogue entries do not create export-coverage failures.

Keep missing input, missing source record, missing property value, no match and ambiguity distinct.

Preserve source and target values, the selected mapping, catalogue revisions and correspondence-file checksums.

The caller decides whether unresolved results block a field, row or export; no implicit unknown value is substituted.

## Delivery scopes

Scope 1 uses one explicitly selected mapping configuration for the source and target versions.

Country and programme variants, selection and overrides belong to scope 2.

Business-rule configuration and output bindings are separate exporter contracts.
